subject: One-off billing shelf credit approval for service lag
messages:
From: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@acmetech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmetech.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency on /generate during peak window — asking for remediation and billing credit

Hi Marcus,

We had a repeat incident this past Friday where our peak traffic between 10:30–11:10 PST experienced elevated p95/p99 latency. Our engineers saw a 6–8x increase in token latency for a subset of requests and that impacted customer-facing search sessions. We raised a ticket with your support team (INC-8893) and got a mitigation, but the window lasted ~40 minutes.

Given the user impact and the fact this was during a paid production run, can Redwood propose a remediation (one-time credit or other makegood)? Procurement is asking for an estimate of the credit amount and the approvals required to finalize.

Attached: ops-incident-summary.pdf — short incident timeline from our side.

Thanks,
Aisha Kumar
Head of Platform, AcmeTech
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: High tail latency on /generate during peak window — credit request (INC-8893)

Karthik / Vanessa — looping you both for exec sign-off path.

Quick summary: AcmeTech saw ~40m elevated latency p95/p99 on Friday morning, customer forwarded their incident timeline (attached). Support confirmed an autoscaler regen and an overloaded GPU queue during a burst that hit our policy route; no data loss, but customer impact is material.

Proposed options (internal):
- Option A: one-time invoice credit = 15% of May usage (~$18k) applied to next invoice — aligns with precedent for 30–60m outages with collateral impact.
- Option B: $12k shelf credit + 2 months of increased rate-limiting headroom (no charge) to help them shift traffic patterns.
- Option C: goodwill: full month pro-rated credit (conservative cap) — requires exec approval; large customer ask.

Attachments: ops-incident-summary.pdf, proposed-credit-breakdown.xlsx

Can you advise which option we can approve at your level, and whether this needs a C-level notification? Need final wording to respond to Aisha and procurement.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: High tail latency on /generate during peak window — credit request (INC-8893)

Thanks Marcus — reviewed the incident notes and the cost modeling in the spreadsheet. A few behavioral notes: AcmeTech is on a reserved-dedicated plan with burst capacity; the incident was partly caused by an unexpected burst pattern that bypassed prefix caching.

Recommendation: Approve Option B ($12k shelf credit + 2 months of no-cost burst headroom capped at current monthly committed units). Rationale: balances customer goodwill and sets a bounded precedent.

Approvals needed: Vanessa (you have budget authority up to $15k for one-offs). If you can sign off, I will finalize the templated credit letter and route DocuSign. If you prefer A/B tweak, indicate changes.

Cc: Marcus so he can update AcmeTech.

-Karthik
VP, Customer Success (in practice)
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: High tail latency on /generate during peak window — credit request (INC-8893)

Approved.

Approve Option B: issue a one-time shelf credit of $12,000 and enable two months of no-cost burst headroom (cap = their current monthly committed units). Please prepare the credit memo with these bullets:
- Credit amount: $12,000 applied to next invoice.
- Burst headroom: two calendar months starting June 1, 2027; subject to current committed units cap.
- No admission of fault; service-level description will remain as-is.
- Attach incident summary and docsign link for AcmeTech signature.

Marcus: send AcmeTech the formal offer and DocuSign link (I signed off on budget). Copy finance for ledger entry.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

-----Original Message-----
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Kumar <aisha.kumar@acmetech.com>, Sam Lee <sam.lee@acmetech.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: One-off credit and burst headroom offer for Friday incident (INC-8893)

Hi Aisha / Sam —

Thanks again for the incident timeline and patience while we reviewed this internally. We want to make this right quickly. Per internal approvals, Redwood will offer the following:

- One-time shelf credit: $12,000 applied to your next invoice.
- Two months of no-cost burst headroom (June 1 — July 31, 2027) capped at your current committed units.

We will send a short credit memo and DocuSign for a quick acknowledgement (no admission of fault). Attachments: proposed-credit-breakdown.xlsx, docsign-acmetech-approval-link.txt

Can you confirm acceptance and the preferred signatory for DocuSign? If procurement prefers a PO reference, let me know and we'll include it.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
